selected.name: Gold-Bond Defensive Pair Switch
selected.description: Monthly: compare trailing 3-month total return of GLD vs AGG (bonds); hold whichever is stronger as a defensive-pair allocation.
selected.signal_rule: Monthly rebalance. score(GLD)=3mo total return, score(AGG)=3mo total return. Hold the higher-scoring of the two, 100% weight, for the next month.
selected.source: SSRN Flight-to-Safety Assets and Volatility Regimes (agent-loop discovery, 2026-07-06)

selected.name: Low-Volatility Sector Tilt
selected.description: Monthly: rank the 11 sector SPDRs by trailing 60-day realized volatility (ascending); hold the 3 LOWEST-vol sectors equal-weight.
selected.signal_rule: Monthly rebalance. Compute 60-trading-day stdev of daily returns per sector. Hold the 3 lowest-vol sectors, equal weight. ALSO compute equal-weight-hold-all-11 as a bias-neutral null benchmark alongside SPY.
selected.source: SSRN The Volatility Effect - Blitz and van Vliet (agent-loop discovery, 2026-07-06)

selected.name: TLT Calendar/Volatility Contraction Breakout
selected.description: On TLT: detect volatility contraction (today's high-low range under 60% of its trailing 20-day average range), then enter long on a breakout above the prior 10-day high; exit after 10 trading days or if price falls below the contraction-period low.
selected.signal_rule: Daily. contraction = (h-l) < 0.6 * avg(h-l, last 20d). If contraction flagged AND close breaks above 10-day high, enter long next bar. Exit after 10 trading days held, or stop if close is below the low of the contraction bar.
selected.source: Practitioner - Toby Crabel volatility-contraction style, trading Twitter (agent-loop discovery, 2026-07-06)

selected.name: Oil-Energy Lead-Lag
selected.description: Test whether USO's trailing return leads XLE's forward return: monthly, if USO's trailing 1-month return is positive, hold XLE for the next month; if negative, hold cash (BIL).
selected.signal_rule: Monthly rebalance using prior month close-to-close return of USO. If usoRet>0 hold XLE next month; if usoRet<=0 hold BIL (cash) next month.
selected.source: SSRN Commodity Price Momentum and Equity Sector Returns (agent-loop discovery, 2026-07-06)

selected.name: Cross-Asset Correlation Regime Filter
selected.description: Monitor rolling 60-day correlation between SPY and TLT daily returns. When correlation is POSITIVE (diversification-fails regime, stocks and bonds falling together), hold cash (BIL) instead of SPY; when correlation is negative (normal regime), hold SPY.
selected.signal_rule: Daily signal using yesterday-and-earlier data only (no lookahead): compute 60-day rolling correlation of SPY vs TLT daily returns as of yesterday. If corr(t-1) > 0, hold BIL today; else hold SPY today.
selected.source: Seeking Alpha - When Stocks and Bonds Move Together (agent-loop discovery, 2026-07-06)

selected.name: Sector Dispersion Mean Reversion
selected.description: Weekly: rank the 11 sector SPDRs by trailing 1-week return; go long the bottom-3 laggards equal-weight for the following week, expecting short-term reversion.
selected.signal_rule: Weekly rebalance (every Monday or first trading day of week). Rank by trailing 5-trading-day return, ascending. Hold bottom-3 (biggest laggards), equal weight, for the next 5 trading days.
selected.source: SSRN Short-Term Reversals in Industry Portfolios (agent-loop discovery, 2026-07-06)

selected.name: Gold Momentum with Trend Confirmation
selected.description: On GLD: buy when trailing 3-month momentum is positive AND price is above its 200-day SMA (trend confirmation gate); sell when momentum turns negative or price crosses below the 200-day SMA.
selected.signal_rule: Daily check using data through yesterday. mom = close[t-1]/close[t-63]-1. If not holding and mom>0 and close[t-1]>SMA200[t-1], buy at today open/close. If holding and (mom<=0 or close[t-1]<SMA200[t-1]), sell.
selected.source: Practitioner - CQG precious-metals trend-following case study (agent-loop discovery, 2026-07-06)

selected.name: Factor Momentum Carousel (Top-2-of-5)
selected.description: Monthly cross-sectional rotation among the five major single-factor ETFs, holding whichever two have had the strongest trailing 6-month total return.
selected.signal_rule: On the first trading day of each month, compute each of MTUM/VLUE/QUAL/USMV/SIZE's trailing 126-trading-day total return. Rank descending. Hold the top 2, equal-weight (50/50), rebalancing monthly. If fewer than 2 ETFs have a positive 126-day return, allocate the shortfall to SPY instead.
selected.source: Ehsani & Linnainmaa (2022), 'Factor Momentum and the Momentum Factor', Journal of Finance

selected.name: Quality-Minus-Junk Static Tilt vs SPY
selected.description: A static (non-rotating) permanent overweight of the Quality factor ETF against SPY, rebalanced back to target quarterly.
selected.signal_rule: Maintain a fixed 60% QUAL / 40% SPY portfolio. On the first trading day of each calendar quarter, compute current dollar weights; if QUAL's weight has drifted more than 5 percentage points from 60%, rebalance both legs back to exactly 60/40.
selected.source: Asness, Frazzini, Pedersen (2013/2019), 'Quality Minus Junk'

selected.name: Low-Vol Regime Switch (USMV/SPY by Realized Volatility Regime)
selected.description: Overweights the low-volatility factor ETF only when the market is in a high-realized-volatility regime, reverting to full SPY exposure when calm.
selected.signal_rule: Each trading day, compute SPY's 20-day realized volatility (annualized) and compare to its trailing 252-day average. If today's 20-day realized vol > 1.25x the 252-day average, hold 100% USMV. Otherwise hold 100% SPY. Only execute a switch if the regime signal persists for 3 consecutive trading days.
selected.source: Frazzini & Pedersen (2014), 'Betting Against Beta'

selected.name: Commodity Basket Time-Series Momentum (Vol-Scaled)
selected.description: TSMOM applied across a basket of commodity ETFs: each asset independently long or flat based on its own trailing return sign, position size scaled inversely to realized volatility.
selected.signal_rule: For each symbol, compute 12mo total return. If positive AND price above 200d SMA, target position = fixed_risk_budget / (20d realized vol annualized); else go flat/cash. Rebalance monthly, recompute vol weekly.
selected.source: Moskowitz/Ooi/Pedersen 2012 'Time Series Momentum'

selected.name: Cross-Sectional Commodity Momentum Rotation (Top-N of Basket)
selected.description: Rank the commodity basket by trailing momentum and hold only the top 3, equal-weight, monthly.
selected.signal_rule: Monthly, rank each ETF by ensembled score = average of 6mo and 12mo total return. Hold top 3, equal-weight. Any candidate whose 12mo return is negative is excluded even if top-3, replaced by cash/BIL.
selected.source: Erb & Harvey 2006 'The Strategic and Tactical Value of Commodity Futures'

selected.name: Gold/Silver Ratio (GSR) Mean-Reversion Rotation
selected.description: Trade the relative-value spread between gold and silver: when gold is historically expensive vs silver, rotate toward silver expecting reversion, and vice versa.
selected.signal_rule: Compute ratio R = Close(GLD)/Close(SLV) and its 252-day z-score. If z > +1.5, hold 100% SLV. If z < -1.5, hold 100% GLD. Between -1.5 and +1.5, hold prior allocation (or 50/50 if no prior). Rebalance weekly on z-score cross.
selected.source: Gold/silver ratio mean-reversion trade in commodity RV literature

selected.name: Momentum-Slope Duration Ladder (TLT/IEF/SHY)
selected.description: Proxies yield-curve-slope regime from relative 3-month price momentum of long vs short duration Treasury ETFs, rotating fully into whichever duration bucket that momentum favors.
selected.signal_rule: Compute 63-day total return for TLT, IEF, SHY. If TLT has the highest 63d return AND it is > 0, hold 100% TLT. Else if IEF has the highest 63d return AND > 0, hold 100% IEF. Else hold 100% SHY. Rebalance monthly on first trading day; only switch if new top-ranked ETF's return exceeds current holding's by more than 1%.
selected.source: Duration-timing / curve-momentum literature

selected.name: Credit Spread Regime Rotation (HYG vs IEF proxy spread)
selected.description: Uses relative price ratio of HYG to IEF as a daily proxy for credit spread direction; rotates between HYG (risk-on) and IEF (risk-off).
selected.signal_rule: Compute ratio R = Close(HYG)/Close(IEF) daily and its 20-day SMA. If R > 20d SMA AND R's 5-day slope is positive, hold 100% HYG. If R < 20d SMA, hold 100% IEF. Check weekly (every Monday); require signal to persist 2 consecutive weekly checks before switching.
selected.source: Credit-spread regime timing concept from credit-cycle literature

selected.name: Inflation Breakeven Momentum Rotation (TIP vs IEF)
selected.description: Uses relative momentum between TIP and IEF as a daily-tradeable breakeven-inflation-expectations proxy, rotating into TIP when inflation expectations rise and IEF when falling.
selected.signal_rule: Compute 90-day return for TIP and IEF. If Return90(TIP) - Return90(IEF) > 0.5%, hold 100% TIP; if < -0.5%, hold 100% IEF; otherwise hold prior allocation. Rebalance monthly on first trading day.
selected.source: Breakeven-inflation rotation concept, standard in real-return fund literature

selected.name: Cross-Sectional Regional Momentum Top-3-of-8
selected.description: Rank a broad set of country/region ETFs by ensembled multi-lookback momentum and hold the top 3 equal-weight, rotating monthly.
selected.signal_rule: Each month-end, compute momentum score per ETF = average of (12mo, 6mo, 3mo return). Rank all 8; hold top 3 equal-weight (33% each), only if score positive AND price > 200d SMA. If fewer than 3 pass, hold passing ones plus cash/BIL for remainder. Rebalance monthly.
selected.source: Extension of Faber/Antonacci cross-sectional momentum to country ETFs

selected.name: Developed-vs-Emerging Regime Rotation (EFA/EEM Relative Strength Switch with Absolute Gate)
selected.description: A binary regime rotation between developed international (EFA) and emerging markets (EEM), switching based on relative 6-12mo momentum, with an absolute-return gate versus cash.
selected.signal_rule: Each month-end compute ensembled momentum (avg of 6mo and 12mo return) for EFA and EEM. If both negative, hold 100% BIL. Otherwise hold whichever has higher momentum, 100%. Rebalance monthly.
selected.source: Antonacci GEM methodology applied to developed/emerging spread

selected.name: Regional Mean-Reversion Pullback-in-Uptrend (RSI(2) Overlay on Country ETFs)
selected.description: Applies Connors RSI(2) short-term mean-reversion logic cross-sectionally across a basket of country ETFs, buying the single most oversold regional ETF that remains in a long-term uptrend.
selected.signal_rule: Daily, for each ETF with close above its 200d SMA, compute 2-day RSI. Select the ETF with lowest RSI(2), provided value is below 10. Buy that ETF with full sleeve notional. Hold until close rises above its 5-day SMA (exit) or price closes below its 200d SMA (stop). If no ETF has RSI(2)<10, stay in cash/BIL.
selected.source: Connors RSI(2) extended cross-sectionally to international ETFs

selected.name: Static Inverse-Volatility Risk Parity (SPY/TLT/GLD/DBC)
selected.description: A monthly-rebalanced risk parity book: each asset's weight set inversely proportional to its trailing realized volatility, targeting equal risk contribution.
selected.signal_rule: Each rebalance date, compute each asset's 20-day daily log-return stdev, annualize (x sqrt(252)) to get vol_i. Raw weight w_i = 1/vol_i, normalize so sum(w_i)=1. Trade to target weights, no leverage, always 100% invested. Rebalance monthly; also rebalance if any asset's weight drifts >20% relative from target.
selected.source: Asness/Frazzini/Pedersen 'Leverage Aversion and Risk Parity', 2012 FAJ

selected.name: All-Weather Static Risk-Balanced Allocation
selected.description: Dalio All Weather concept with liquid ETF proxies: fixed strategic weight split across growth-equity, long-duration bonds, intermediate bonds, gold, and commodities.
selected.signal_rule: Fixed target weights: SPY 30%, TLT 40%, IEF 15%, GLD 7.5%, DBC 7.5%. On each rebalance date compute current portfolio weights and trade any asset whose weight has drifted more than 5 percentage points absolute from target back to target.
selected.frequency: quarterly rebalance with 5pp drift-band check monthly
selected.source: Ray Dalio / Bridgewater 'All Weather' portfolio

selected.name: Equal Risk Contribution (ERC) Two-Asset Barbell: SPY/TLT
selected.description: A tighter stock/bond risk parity barbell using a shorter, more responsive 10-day vol window rebalanced weekly.
selected.signal_rule: Compute 10-day trailing annualized realized vol for SPY and TLT separately. Weight_SPY = (1/vol_SPY)/(1/vol_SPY + 1/vol_TLT); Weight_TLT = 1 - Weight_SPY. Rebalance weekly (every Monday) to these target weights regardless of drift size.
selected.source: Stock/bond risk-parity barbell, common simplified risk-parity implementation

selected.name: Classic 12-Month TSMOM Multi-Asset Sleeve
selected.description: Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen time-series momentum applied independently to five liquid ETFs spanning equities, bonds, gold, commodities, and the dollar.
selected.signal_rule: On first trading day of each month, for each asset independently compute r_12 = close_today/close_252_days_ago - 1. If r_12 > 0, hold a 1/5 equal-weight position for the month; if r_12 <= 0, hold cash (BIL) for that slot instead.
selected.source: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012), 'Time Series Momentum'

selected.name: Dual Moving-Average Crossover Trend Sleeve
selected.description: Each asset uses a fast/slow moving-average crossover to decide long-vs-flat, independently per asset, across a five-asset multi-class universe.
selected.signal_rule: For each asset independently compute 50-day SMA and 200-day SMA. Hold 1/5 equal-weight long when SMA50 > SMA200; go flat/cash when SMA50 <= SMA200. Trade only on the day the crossover state flips for that asset.
selected.frequency: daily check, trades on crossover-flip days
selected.source: Clenow, 'Following the Trend'; dual-MA trend-following

selected.name: Skip-Month TSMOM (12-1 Momentum, Trend Version)
selected.description: Applies the 'skip the most recent month' refinement to the multi-asset TSMOM sleeve: signal based on months t-12 to t-1 rather than t-12 to t, independently per asset.
selected.signal_rule: On first trading day of each month, for each asset independently compute r_12_1 = close_21_days_ago/close_252_days_ago - 1. If r_12_1 > 0, hold 1/5 equal-weight long for the month; else flat/cash.
selected.source: Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) skip-month convention applied to TSMOM

selected.name: Donchian Turtle Breakout
selected.description: Classic Turtle-style dual Donchian channel breakout: enter long on a new 20-day high breakout, exit on a new 10-day low, with ATR-based stop.
selected.signal_rule: Compute 20-day rolling high (excluding today) as entry_high and 10-day rolling low (excluding today) as exit_low. BUY when close > entry_high(20) AND no existing position. Initial stop = entry_price - 2*ATR(20). SELL when close < exit_low(10), or close < trailing stop (new_stop = max(current_stop, close - 2*ATR(20)), recalculated daily, only moves up). Skip re-entry for 1 day after a stopped-out exit.
selected.source: Donchian channel breakout / Turtle Trading System 1

selected.name: Keltner Squeeze Breakout
selected.description: Volatility-squeeze breakout: identify low-volatility consolidation (Bollinger Bands inside Keltner Channel), then enter in the direction of the breakout once the squeeze fires.
selected.signal_rule: Keltner Channel = 20-day EMA +/- 1.5*ATR(20). Bollinger Bands = 20-day SMA +/- 2*stdev(20). Squeeze ON when upper_BB < upper_KC AND lower_BB > lower_KC. BUY on first bar squeeze turns OFF AND close > upper_KC AND 12-bar linear-regression momentum of typical price is positive. Initial stop = lower_KC at entry. SELL when close < middle EMA(20) or stop hit; stop trails up daily to max(prior_stop, current_lower_KC).
selected.source: Bollinger-inside-Keltner 'squeeze' popularized by John Carter (TTM Squeeze)

selected.name: Supertrend Flip System
selected.description: ATR-band Supertrend indicator flips between long-stop and short-stop bands; used long-only, buying on bullish flips and exiting on bearish flips.
selected.signal_rule: ATR period 10, multiplier 3.0. basic_upper=(H+L)/2+3*ATR(10); basic_lower=(H+L)/2-3*ATR(10). final_upper/final_lower tighten toward price in the trend direction only (standard Supertrend ratchet rule). BUY when close crosses above the current Supertrend line (bullish flip). SELL (full exit) when close crosses below the Supertrend line (bearish flip).
selected.source: Supertrend indicator, standard 10-period/3x-ATR parameterization

selected.name: ADX-Filtered Trend Entry
selected.description: Wilder's ADX used as a trend-strength gate combined with a directional-movement crossover entry, avoiding trades in non-trending regimes.
selected.signal_rule: Compute +DI(14), -DI(14), ADX(14) per Wilder. BUY when ADX(14) > 25 AND +DI(14) crosses above -DI(14). Initial stop = entry_price - 2.5*ATR(14). SELL when +DI crosses back below -DI, OR ADX(14) falls below 20, OR trailing stop (ratcheted up daily to close - 2.5*ATR(14), never lowered) is breached.
selected.source: Average Directional Index (ADX) / J. Welles Wilder

selected.name: Halloween Indicator / Sell-in-May Seasonality
selected.description: Classic six-month seasonal cycle: long SPY only Nov 1-Apr 30, in BIL/cash May 1-Oct 31.
selected.signal_rule: On the first trading day of November, rotate 100% into SPY. On the first trading day of May, rotate 100% into BIL. Repeat annually. No intra-period trading.
selected.source: Bouman & Jacobsen (2002) 'The Halloween Indicator'

selected.name: Santa Claus Rally (Last 5 + First 2 Trading Days)
selected.description: Long-only exposure limited to the last 5 trading days of December plus the first 2 trading days of January.
selected.signal_rule: Using the trading calendar, identify the last 5 trading days of each calendar year and first 2 trading days of the following January. Go long at the close 5 trading days before year-end; exit at the close of the 2nd trading day of January. Flat all other days.
selected.source: Yale Hirsch, Stock Trader's Almanac

selected.name: Pre-Holiday Drift
selected.description: US equities historically show abnormally positive returns on the trading day immediately preceding a market holiday. Test being long SPY/QQQ only on that day.
selected.signal_rule: Using the NYSE holiday calendar, identify the last trading session before each of the 9 annual market holidays. Enter long at prior day's close, exit at that session's close. Flat all other sessions. Compare average per-trade return and hit rate to an equal-count random-day control sample.
selected.source: Ariel (1990) 'High Stock Returns before Holidays'

selected.name: Yield-Curve-Slope Cyclical/Defensive Switch
selected.description: Uses relative momentum of long vs short-duration Treasury ETFs as a proxy for yield-curve steepening/flattening to gate exposure between cyclical and defensive sector baskets.
selected.signal_rule: Compute curve_proxy = 63d return(TLT) - 63d return(SHY). If curve_proxy > 0, hold equal-weight cyclical basket (XLI, XLK, XLY, XLF); if < 0, hold equal-weight defensive basket (XLP, XLU, XLV). Rebalance only on regime flips confirmed for 2 consecutive days.
selected.frequency: daily signal check, rebalance on confirmed regime flip
selected.source: Yield-curve recession-signal literature adapted to an ETF-tradeable momentum proxy

selected.name: Utilities-vs-Discretionary Recession-Risk Sector Rotator
selected.description: XLU/XLY relative strength is a known market-internals recession-risk tell; uses its trend to gate a cyclical-vs-defensive basket rotation.
selected.signal_rule: Compute ratio = price(XLU)/price(XLY). Compute ratio_ma50 and ratio_ma200. If ratio_ma50 < ratio_ma200 (risk-on), hold equal-weight cyclical basket {XLK, XLF, XLI}. If ratio_ma50 > ratio_ma200 (risk-off), hold equal-weight defensive basket {XLP, XLV, XLU}. Act only on new MA crossovers.
selected.frequency: daily monitoring, rebalance on MA crossover events only
selected.source: XLU/XLY as a market-internals recession-risk indicator

selected.name: Gold/Cyclical-Metals Inflation-Regime Sector Tilt
selected.description: Uses relative momentum between GLD and tech as an inflation-regime proxy, tilting toward inflation-beneficiary sectors vs low-inflation-beneficiary sectors.
selected.signal_rule: Compute infl_proxy = 126d return(GLD) - 126d return(XLK). If infl_proxy > 0, hold equal-weight {XLE, XLB}. If infl_proxy <= 0, hold equal-weight {XLK, XLY}. Rebalance monthly; hold basket until sign of infl_proxy flips on a monthly rebalance date.
selected.source: Gold-as-inflation-regime-indicator + cyclical/growth sector sensitivity to inflation regimes

selected.name: Dividend-Yield-Spread Regime Tilt (SCHD vs SPY)
selected.description: Rotates between SCHD and SPY based on relative risk-adjusted momentum (return/volatility), favoring dividend-quality only when it wins on a risk-adjusted basis.
selected.signal_rule: Compute rolling 126-day return and rolling 63-day realized volatility for both SCHD and SPY. Compute score = return/volatility for each. If SCHD's score exceeds SPY's by more than 0.1, hold 100% SCHD; if SPY's exceeds SCHD's by more than 0.1, hold 100% SPY; otherwise hold prior position. Rebalance monthly.
selected.source: Risk-adjusted relative strength (a la dual momentum) applied within-equity-style

selected.name: Dividend-Aristocrat Low-Vol Breadth Tilt (NOBL/VYM basket vs SPY)
selected.description: Rotates between a basket of dividend ETFs and SPY based on which single dividend ETF shows lowest realized volatility combined with a positive trend.
selected.signal_rule: Each month, compute 63-day realized vol and check price > 200d SMA for NOBL, VYM, DVY, SDY. Filter to those above their 200d SMA. Among survivors, select the ETF with lowest 63-day realized vol and hold it 100%. If none pass, hold SPY. Rebalance monthly.
selected.source: Low-volatility factor selection applied cross-sectionally within the dividend-ETF category

selected.name: Dividend ETF Drawdown-Triggered Defensive Switch
selected.description: Uses SPY's own drawdown from its rolling 1-year high as the trigger to shift into SCHD for shallower drawdowns and lower beta, shifting back once SPY has recovered.
selected.signal_rule: Track SPY's rolling 252-day high. Compute drawdown = (SPY close / rolling 252d high) - 1. If drawdown crosses below -10%, switch to 100% SCHD. Remain until SPY's close recovers to within 2% of a new rolling 252-day high, then switch back to 100% SPY. Check daily, trade only on state transitions.
selected.source: Drawdown-state-machine defensive rotation design

selected.name: Financials Breadth Pairs (XLF/KRE)
selected.description: Broad financials vs regional banks stat-arb: regional banks carry more idiosyncratic credit/rate-sensitivity risk so the spread mean-reverts around macro financial-sector cycles.
selected.signal_rule: Compute spread = ln(XLF)-ln(KRE). Compute rolling 60-day mean and std of spread. z=(spread-mean60)/std60. Enter short-XLF/long-KRE when z>+2.0; enter long-XLF/short-KRE when z<-2.0. Exit both legs when |z|<0.5. Hard stop-out (close position, no re-entry same week) if |z|>3.5. Dollar-neutral 50/50 notional.
selected.source: Standard sector-vs-subsector stat-arb

selected.name: Biotech Sub-Index Pairs (XBI/IBB)
selected.description: XBI (equal-weight, small/mid-cap biotech) vs IBB (cap-weighted, large-cap biotech/pharma) — weighting-methodology divergence produces a mean-reverting spread.
selected.signal_rule: spread = ln(XBI)-ln(IBB). Rolling 50-day mean/std. z=(spread-mean50)/std50. Enter long-XBI/short-IBB when z<-1.75; enter short-XBI/long-IBB when z>+1.75. Exit at |z|<0.4. Stop-out and flatten if |z|>3.0 or either ETF gaps >8% overnight. Dollar-neutral notional daily.
selected.source: Sub-index methodology divergence (equal-weight vs cap-weight) within same sector

selected.name: Semiconductors vs Broad Tech (SMH/XLK)
selected.description: SMH is a pure-play semiconductor bet (cyclical) while XLK is broad tech (software-heavy, more secular); the ratio oscillates with the semiconductor cycle.
selected.signal_rule: spread = ln(SMH)-ln(XLK). Rolling 45-day mean/std. z=(spread-mean45)/std45. Long-SMH/short-XLK when z<-2.0; short-SMH/long-XLK when z>+2.0. Exit both legs at |z|<0.5. Stop-out if |z|>3.5. Dollar-neutral notional, rebalanced weekly.
selected.source: Cyclical sub-sector (semis) vs secular broad-sector divergence

selected.name: Realized-Vol Position-Sizing Overlay on Core SPY
selected.description: A risk overlay scaling notional of a long-SPY sleeve inversely to trailing realized volatility, targeting constant risk contribution.
selected.signal_rule: Compute 20-day annualized realized vol RV_t from SPY daily log returns. Target annual vol T=12%. Position weight w_t = clip(T/RV_t, 0.5, 1.5) applied to notional SPY exposure, rebalanced weekly. No entry/exit signal — always long, scaled.
selected.source: Moreira & Muir (2017) 'Volatility-Managed Portfolios'

selected.name: Fear-Gauge Divergence De-Risking Signal
selected.description: Detects bearish divergence: SPY prints a new 20-day high while trailing realized volatility rises rather than falls; on divergence, cuts SPY sleeve exposure by a fixed haircut for a cooldown window.
selected.signal_rule: SPY makes a new 20-day closing high on day t. Compute 10-day realized vol RV_10 and compare to RV_10 from 10 trading days earlier. Divergence flag = (SPY_close_t equals max(SPY_close,20d)) AND (RV_10_t > RV_10_t-10 * 1.15). On flag, reduce SPY sleeve weight to 60% for the next 10 trading days or until RV_10 falls back below its flag-time level, whichever first, then restore to 100%.
selected.source: Divergence/complacency warning-signal literature

selected.name: Realized-Vol Regime Filter for Sector Momentum Sizing
selected.description: An overlay scaling the already-live sector_momentum.py basket's aggregate notional down during high-realized-vol regimes and back up during calm regimes, without touching the selection logic.
selected.signal_rule: Compute SPY 63-day realized vol RV_63 and its 252-day rolling median M. Regime = 'high' if RV_63 > 1.3*M, else 'normal'. In 'high' regime, scale total sector-basket notional to 50%; in 'normal', 100%. Reassess monthly alongside the sector_momentum rebalance date.
selected.source: Volatility-scaled momentum overlays (Barroso & Santa-Clara 2015, 'Momentum has its Moments')

selected.name: Growth-Value Relative Momentum Switch (IWF/IWD)
selected.description: Binary rotation into whichever Russell 1000 style sleeve (growth or value) has had stronger trailing total-return momentum, re-balanced monthly.
selected.signal_rule: On the first trading day of each month, compute ensembled momentum score = average of (12mo, 6mo, 3mo return) for IWF and IWD. Hold 100% of whichever has the higher score. If both scores are negative, hold BIL instead.
selected.source: Adaptation of Antonacci-style dual momentum applied to the growth/value style factor

selected.name: Growth/Value Ratio Trend-Following (Moving Average Crossover)
selected.description: Treats the IWF/IWD price ratio as a single trending series and follows its trend with a fast/slow SMA crossover.
selected.signal_rule: Compute daily ratio R = Close(IWF)/Close(IWD). Compute SMA20(R) and SMA100(R). When SMA20 crosses above SMA100, rotate 100% into IWF; when SMA20 crosses below SMA100, rotate 100% into IWD. Trades only occur on crossover days.
selected.source: Time-series momentum applied to a relative-price ratio series

selected.name: 52-Week Relative-High Breakout Style Switch
selected.description: Rotates into whichever style ETF is closer to its own 52-week high relative to the other, treating proximity-to-high as a stand-in for persistent leadership.
selected.signal_rule: Daily, compute for each ETF: pct_from_high = Close / rolling_252d_max(Close) - 1. Hold whichever ETF currently has the higher (less negative) pct_from_high. Switch only when the ranking flips and persists for 3 consecutive days.
selected.frequency: daily signal check with 3-day confirmation filter
selected.source: 52-week-high proximity as a momentum/strength proxy (George & Hwang, 2004)

selected.name: Gap-Fill Fade
selected.description: Fades the opening gap when a stock/ETF opens away from prior close, betting the session reverts toward yesterday's close.
selected.signal_rule: Each day at the open, compute gap = (Open - PriorClose)/PriorClose. If gap < -0.30% (gap down), buy at the open, exit at that day's close; skip entry on gap-up days (long-only). Require |gap| >= 0.30% to filter noise-level gaps. Track whether Close is closer to PriorClose than Open was as the fill-rate metric.
selected.source: Documented gap-fill/gap-fade microstructure literature

selected.name: 3-Day Losing/Winning Streak Reversal
selected.description: Mean-reversion on short consecutive-day streaks: after exactly 3 consecutive down closes in an uptrend, buy expecting a bounce.
selected.signal_rule: Count consecutive daily closes below the prior close. On the close of the 3rd consecutive down day, if Close > 200-day SMA, buy at next open. Exit when the ETF has one up-close day (Close > prior Close) OR after a max hold of 5 trading days, whichever comes first.
selected.source: Streak/run-length reversal studies (Connors-style research)

selected.name: Narrow-Range Compression Breakout (NR7)
selected.description: Volatility-contraction pattern: identify the narrowest daily range in the last 7 days (NR7) as a coiled-spring signal, then trade the breakout of that day's range the next session.
selected.signal_rule: Each day, compute daily range = High-Low. Flag NR7 when today's range is the smallest of the trailing 7 days. On an NR7 day, set buy-stop at NR7-day High for the next trading day. If next-day High triggers the buy-stop, go long at that price. Exit long on close below the 10-day SMA or after a 10-day max hold.
selected.source: NR7 volatility-contraction pattern (Toby Crabel-style range contraction)
